prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.45
  tan: 0.55
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
- Core stance: UKIP, founded in 1993, seeks UK withdrawal from the EU to restore full national sovereignty. It would repeal the European Communities Act (1972), keep the pound permanently, protect British common law (jury trial, presumption of innocence), and oppose an EU government, army, and constitution.

- Economy: Leave the EU to pursue global free trade, deepen Commonwealth/US ties, and regain an independent WTO voice. Claims inward investment will remain due to UK strengths. Major deregulation, especially for small firms, including scrapping burdensome EU-derived rules (e.g., compulsory metrication). Independence Dividend estimated at about £20bn per year from ending EU budget payments and gains from growth, bureaucracy cuts, and fisheries. Planned use: agriculture £2bn; regional support £1bn; state pension +£5/week (£2.8bn), elderly care £0.5bn, restore frozen expat pensions £0.3bn; tax cuts for low paid £1.4bn; family/IHT/CGT reforms £1.3bn; NHS +£2bn and nurses £0.5bn; 30,000 teachers £1.2bn; 25,000 police £0.8bn; fuel duty −9p/litre (£3.7bn); defence +£2.5bn. Tax policy: raise income tax threshold; simplify/self-assessment and VAT overhaul (consider retail sales tax outside EU); remove main home from IHT; oppose EU tax harmonisation. Keep Bank of England independence.

- Health and welfare: Decentralise NHS management, restore matron roles, raise nurse pay, recruit globally post-EU, cut bureaucracy. Overhaul social services culture. Simplify benefits so work always pays; consider basic income for specific groups (e.g., long-term workers, single parents). Restore married couple tax allowance for families. Long term, shift part of NI into funded personal pensions; protect current pensioners.

- Education: Emphasise basics; allow selection/streaming; target class sizes under 25; hire more teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; reform teacher training; curb politicisation/EU propaganda; protect school sports and stop playing-field sales; consider vouchers and private provision with access safeguards.

- Transport and environment: Pragmatic, case-by-case transport policy; oppose partial sell‑off of London Underground; cut fuel duty; fund roads, rail maintenance, cycle lanes; encourage integrated transport. Environmental approach: local accountability, simpler enforcement, market-led solutions with fair rules; support renewables (biofuels, wave, wind, solar, hydrogen); strict GMO labelling and consumer protection; local health-focused monitoring.

- Home affairs: Reject EU Corpus Juris and Europol encroachments; repeal and re-enact Human Rights Act to align with British common law; oppose EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. More police, focus on visible community policing; deterrent sentencing with rehabilitation options; “life means life” for heinous crimes. Immigration policy set solely by UK; skills-based admissions; fair but firm asylum with faster processing and secure reception.

- Agriculture and fisheries: Leave CAP; introduce voluntary Land Management Contract Scheme paying farmers for agreed environmental/social outcomes; support organics and high welfare; enable rural diversification; balanced access to countryside; create a Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. Exit CFP; regain exclusive control (up to 200 miles), use conservation zones, ban damaging methods, and negotiate access bilaterally.

- Defence and foreign affairs: Increase defence funding; exit EU Rapid Reaction Force; prioritise NATO and US interoperability; buy cost-effective US tech; encourage reserves/cadets; targeted aid direct to communities with governance conditions; prefer Council of Europe’s voluntary cooperation model.

- Constitution and governance: Enact a UK Bill of Rights preventing any transfer of sovereignty; strengthen Parliament and Select Committees; curb executive lawmaking and quangos; oppose EU-driven regionalism; preserve two-chamber system; restore county-based local government and boundaries; enable local/national referenda by petition; oppose state funding of political parties.

TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core principles: Freedom, Justice, Honesty. Government should enable people by delivering high‑quality public services, devolving power, and embedding a “green thread” across all policy.

Health:
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, plus 10,000 beds; £1,000 annual pay boost for lowest‑paid NHS staff.
- Prioritise prevention: free dental and eye checks, more scanning equipment, £500m for NHS dentistry, wider in‑practice testing, support complementary medicine.
- End charges for long‑term personal care; create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end the postcode lottery and lower drug costs; aim to reduce/abolish prescription charges.
- Patient Care Guarantees; stronger local accountability; independent advocates; no‑fault compensation; ban age discrimination; end mixed wards.

Education, skills and jobs:
- Primary classes to average 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (focus on Key Stage 1); paid preparation time; teacher training salary; scrap SATs at 7; reduce bureaucracy.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorest; raise loan repayment threshold; improve academic pay equality.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 2 for adults; Level 3 for 16–24s); simpler FE funding/qualifications.
- Replace New Deal with a flexible, combined Benefits and Jobs Agency; study leave with pay for 16–24s; SME training incentives.

Law and order:
- 6,000 extra police; 2,000 part‑time retained community officers; Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent police complaints system.
- Focus prisons on work, skills and rehabilitation; expand effective community sentences; cut reoffending.
- Strengthen victims’ rights; keep jury trial; end most mandatory sentences; tackle hate crime.

Transport:
- Free off‑peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; aim half‑price for under‑19s in education.
- Abolish VED for the cleanest vehicles; no real‑terms fuel duty rise next Parliament; empower congestion charging/parking levies to fund public transport.
- Sustainable Transport Authority; stronger regulation; restructure Railtrack into a public‑interest model; modernise Underground via not‑for‑profit bonds; rural transport fund.
- Double rail freight by 2010; curb road building in sensitive areas; promote cleaner vehicles.

Pensions, wages and benefits:
- Raise basic pension (+£5; more for over‑75/80); create Independent Pensions Authority; relax annuity rules; reduce means‑testing.
- Review minimum wage annually and apply full rate from age 16.
- Extra support for children on long‑term income support; replace CSA with family courts; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled; long‑term goal to zero the 10p tax band for low earners.

Business, consumers and green economy:
- Cut red tape; small business rates allowance; tougher competition law (esp. local monopolies, banking); stronger consumer protection.
- Shift taxes from “goods” to pollution: move toward a carbon tax; 10% UK renewables by 2010 (rising annually); phase out nuclear at end of life; expand energy efficiency.

Constitution and civil liberties:
- Fair votes: AV+ referendum for Westminster (ultimately STV); STV for local/European elections; elected Senate; stronger Parliament and FOI; votes at 16.
- Equality Act and Commission; repeal Section 28; stronger privacy/surveillance safeguards; humane, faster asylum system, end vouchers; more devolution and local income tax.

Communities, rural/urban:
- One‑stop regeneration grants; protect local services; brownfield‑first with VAT/business rate reform; national recycling programme; CAP/CFP reform; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs.

Europe, foreign policy and defence:
- Pro‑EU reform: constitution to define powers, greater transparency, enlargement, stronger CFSP; euro entry via referendum at a sustainable rate.
- End subsidies for arms exports; 0.7% aid target; faster debt relief; fair trade with environmental safeguards; support ICC/UN peacekeeping.
- Maintain defence spending; flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; oppose US NMD.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_D aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_C" | "TEXT_D"
}
